2. The short fact leading to the instant Criminal Miscellaneous Case is that the petitioner, Shudindra Talukder as informant lodged a First Information Report on 7.7.2005 with Sunamganj Police Station alleging inter-alia that he along with his brother, Sattendra Talukder lives together. The accused persons are their neighbor’s and of bad Character. On 3.7.2005 at night when his niece Sanchita Talukder(Saran) daughter of his brother Sattendra Talukder returning to her room after attending the call of nature in a nearby toilet accused’s Abu Laise and Karim armed with deadly weapons pressing her mouth kidnapped forcibly. The informant and his other inmates recognised the accuseds in electric light but did not dare to resist. The informant informed the occurrence to the nearby police camp and searched for the victim girl with the help of police here and there but failed. Thereafter the informant along with other witnesses recovered the victim girl from the house of accused No.8, Rashid Ali of village Tokergaon in senseless condition at 4.30 A.M. on 6.7.2005 and took her to Sylhet for treatment. Upon this ejahar police started Sunamganj Police Station Case No.6 dated 7.7.2005 against 8 accused’s along with another 8/10 unknown accused persons under section 7 read with section 30 of Nan 0 Shishu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000. 

 5. Police after investigation submitted charge sheet on 5.9.2005 against the F.I.R. named accused’s under section 7 read with 30 of the Nari 0 Shishu Niratan Daman Ain, 2000. Thereafter the case was transferred to Nari 0 Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal, Sunamganju and numbered as Nari 0 Shishu Nirjatan Daman Case No.84 of 2005. 

 6. On 4.2.2007 Ganada Talukder wife of .Sattendra Talukder, the mother of the victim filed an application before the Tribunal for releasing the victim from judicial custody and give the victim to her custody contending the victim being a minor she was suffering both physically and mentally. On the same day the victim Shanchita. Talukder also filed an application praying for her release from judicial custody and to go on her self custody stating that she being major was capable of her welfare and that she made the statements before the learned . Magistrate under pressure of her relatives. She further stated that out of her free will converted her religion to Islam and that she was not kidnapped nor tortured by the accused’s. The case has been filed against the accused’s out of previous enmity showing her oppressed by the accused’s. 

 7. The learned Judge of the Tribunal hearing the parties by his order dated 4.2.2007 rejected both the applications filed by the victim as well as her mother and considering the safety of the victim allowed her to remain in the judicial custody. Being aggrieved by the said order the informant filed this case before this court under section 491 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and obtained the present Rule on 14.3.2007. 

 11. The petitioner has challenged the judicial custody of the victim under the provision of section 491 of the. Code of Criminal Procedure considering the impugned order is some kind of detention passed under the veneer of judicial custody. Section 491 of the Code may be invoked to secure justice for those who are detained illegally. As the order under challenge does not bear the legal acumen in its true sense the only course is open to the petitioner for remedy under Section 491 of the Code. In support of our view there are several decisions of our Appellate Division and the High Court Division. Reference may be made to the case of Arun Karmakar Vs. State reported in 7 BLC (AD) 61. 

 12. The cardinal question in this case is required to be determined whether the detenue has attained the age of 18 years or not. From the medical reports dated 11.7.2005 at Annexures-C and D to the application it appears that at the time of occurrence age of the detenue was '16 years 

 14. We have given our anxious consideration which lead us to form opinion that since the detenue is not an accused in this criminal case and by now has attained the age of 18 years, she should be released from the judicial custody to find out her destiny at her own will freely.
